summary.text: A 75-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and hypertension, and no history of perineal or anal disease, presented with a left hemicircumferential adenocarcinoma of the rectum 4 cm above the anal verge. Pelvic MRI and endorectal ultrasound classified the tumor preoperatively as T3, and preoperative workup imaging showed no evidence of distant metastases.

Six weeks after neoadjuvant chemotherapy she underwent a laparoscopic proctectomy with total mesorectal excision and intersphincteric resection. The Lone Star Retractor was used for anal verge exposure, the perineal dissection was transanal, the anal canal was washed with povidone-iodine, a hand-sewn side-to-end coloanal anastomosis was made, and a diverting lateral ileostomy was created.

Pathology showed a well-differentiated adenocarcinoma ypT3N0 with poor therapeutic response Dworak 1, a complete mesorectum, a 5 mm circumferential margin and a 6 mm distal margin; the surgery was considered a curative R0 resection with tumor-free adequate margins. A grade B anastomotic fistula was treated by transanal drainage, the stoma was closed 4 months postoperatively, and no adjuvant chemotherapy was given.

On the fifth postoperative week she developed acute dehydration with functional renal insufficiency and hyperkalemia leading to cardiac arrest, which was resuscitated, and she recovered without visceral damage.

At 14-month follow-up she was in poor general condition with rectal bleeding and right femoropopliteal venous thrombosis. A 2-cm budding lesion on the right of the anal verge arose from perianal skin without continuity with the anastomosis, at a retractor hook insertion site. Digital examination found a local recurrence, CT showed no distant recurrence, and biopsy showed a similar well-differentiated adenocarcinoma. She was not operated because of her general condition and received no further treatment.
